nodes.description: JPH2 deficiency reduces the number of junctional membrane complexes and increases variability of sarcolemmal-to-sarcoplasmic-reticulum spacing in experimental cardiomyocytes. Reduced colocalization of L-type channels with RyR2 impairs excitation-contraction coupling. This structural lesion is distinct from the accompanying defect in RyR2 inactivation; unchanged channel abundance does not imply unchanged channel function.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic JPH2 variants reduce junctophilin-2 function. Reported alleles include truncating variants and less well characterized missense variants; residual protein abundance, localization, and channel interactions may differ by allele. The c.1920dupT allele predicts C-terminal truncation, rather than demonstrating complete protein absence. Impaired membrane tethering and calcium-channel regulation are supported by experimental JPH2 depletion.
